mainEntity.name: What is a B2B SaaS PR agency and who is it for?

acceptedAnswer.text: A B2B SaaS PR agency builds the category narrative, media presence and analyst relationships that shorten enterprise deal cycles. It is for founders selling to buying committees: the VP of Engineering who needs a technical proof point, the CFO who needs a credible market position, and the security team who needs a vendor with a published track record. A fractional senior operator delivers this directly for $5K–$12K/month, without the junior account team a traditional agency charges $15K–$45K/month to staff.

mainEntity.name: How much does B2B SaaS PR cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A traditional B2B PR agency retainer runs $15K–$45K per month because it funds a multi-person account team. A fractional senior operator delivers the same senior scope for $5K–$12K per month, with one experienced person running strategy and pitching editors directly. A focused launch sprint, covering positioning, a wave of tier-1 placements and analyst briefings, runs $15K–$40K over four to eight weeks.

mainEntity.name: Which outlets and deliverables do you focus on for B2B SaaS?

acceptedAnswer.text: Publications mapped to your buying committee: Forbes, TechCrunch, VentureBeat and Fast Company for the mainstream business buyer; The Information and relevant vertical trade press for the practitioner; AI Magazine, Benzinga and Decrypt for AI-native audiences. Analyst briefings for Gartner, Forrester and independent category analysts. Customer case studies placed as contributed articles or cited in news features. Coverage depends on a real news hook or a genuine customer outcome, not a press release blast.

mainEntity.name: What does the process look like and how long before I see results?

acceptedAnswer.text: The first two weeks are narrative teardown and positioning: one ownable category word, a three-sentence company thesis, and a media and analyst map. Weeks three and four are pitching and briefing cadence. First placed stories typically land in week four to six. Sustained tier-1 coverage builds over three to six months as the category narrative gets picked up, quoted and cited. AI engine mentions follow media coverage, usually with a four to eight week lag after placement.

mainEntity.name: How do I get started with Shilika Jain for B2B SaaS PR?

acceptedAnswer.text: Send a short project brief through the intent form and you will get a reply within 24 hours with a quick read on your current press footprint and category position. Or book a 30-minute call and we will map it live. No intro deck, no three-week agency scoping process.
